Figure 1:Overview of InstantFusion.
During training, model-specific LAEs map the intermediate
states of frozen generators into a shared representation
space, where both latent states and denoising dynamics are
aligned.
During inference, a sender state is translated through the
shared space into the receiver’s latent space, and an adaptive
criterion determines when the receiver takes over denoising.

Figure 2:Cross-model compatibility.(a) Intermediate states from Qwen-Image, SD3, and FLUX.1 exhibit similar spatial self-similarity patterns.
(b) Direct handoff between related models preserves generation quality, while cross-family handoff retains the main subject and coarse layout.
(c) These observations motivate a lightweight interface for connecting heterogeneous generators.

Figure 3:Architecture of the LAE.(a)σ\sigmadenotes the scalar noise level associated with
denoising steptkt_{k}. It is spatially broadcast and concatenated with
the intermediate state𝐱tkA\mathbf{x}_{t_{k}}^{A}. Convolutional layers and time-conditioned residual blocks then map the input to its encoded representation𝐳tkA\mathbf{z}_{t_{k}}^{A}, with a skip connection preserving the original state.
(b) Details of the time-conditioned resblock: Each residual block embedsσ\sigmaand predicts scale and shift parameters that modulate group-normalized features, conditioning the transformation on the current denoising stage.

Figure 4:Effect of denoising-dynamics alignment.Training withoutℒdyn\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{dyn}}establishes correspondence between intermediate states𝐱\mathbf{x}, but leaves their associated denoising velocities𝐯\mathbf{v}poorly aligned. Addingℒdyn\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{dyn}}improves velocity alignment. Each line in the UMAP visualization connects the𝐯\mathbf{v}feature points produced by different models when conditioned on the same prompt.

Figure 5:Training dynamics of the model-specific LAEs. The total loss and the three component losses (ℒrec\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{rec}},ℒalign\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}, andℒdyn\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{dyn}}) decrease steadily and converge during training.
Figure 6:Qualitative comparison of Qwen-Image, FLUX.1, and SD3 outputs after 1, 5, and 10 repeated latent round trips. The original outputs before any round trip serve as baselines.
Figure 7:Qualitative results of cross-model latent transfer among heterogeneous generators.
Figure 8:Evolution of generated images over training steps during cross-model OPD.
Figure 9:Comparison between the predicted clean images at adaptively selected handoff steps and the corresponding fully denoised outputs, demonstrating preservation of global structure.
